title: Negative (first pass at 20261026T1334-c42-q-ecology-next, arm a): predators that live long enough to divide at labkit's default 2000 t window (slower decay or satiation) eat the prey out; in 8 variants no run has both kinds dividing at K=20
summary: The claim world of 20261026T1302-c42-foodchain-both-divide-claim (Du 1, chi 0, k0 0.002), seed 0, 128^2, t=12000, labkit default K=20. Lower predator decay kq 0.0025/0.002/0.0015 (claim 0.003): predator persistent splits 8/0/0 (generation 2/0/0) with 36/24/3 predator components at the end, but prey are at 1/0/0 components and 0 prey persistent splits; predators then live on dissolved prey as a near-static emulsion. Satiating predation eat = k2 ca cb^2/(1 + ca/Ksat): Ksat 0.5 with k2 0.5 gives 15 predator persistent splits (generation 3, merge/split 0.55) and 58 predators, but prey are extinct at the end (qa7/sheet.png: prey droplets renucleate and are eaten at once); Ksat 1 with k2 0.3 keeps 8 prey but predators reach 2 persistent splits (generation 1) and prey 0; Ksat 0.3 (k2 0.4) and 0.1 (k2 0.8) starve the predators (0 at the end, prey a frozen emulsion of 65-68); kq 0.0025 with Ksat 0.5 (k2 0.35): predators 4 persistent splits (generation 2), prey extinct. At K=20 the claim's own parameters give predator persistent splits 0. So in this chain a predator droplet that lives > 2000 t between fissions also grazes the dissolved prey well enough to suppress every prey droplet; the coexistence with both kinds dividing in 20261026T1302-c42-foodchain-both-divide-claim rests on short-lived predators (500-1500 t). One seed per variant.
